caseno:
Civil Revision No. 784 of 2007 
with 
Civil Rule No. 364 (R) of 2007 (Violation)
lawyer:
Abu Yahia Dulal, Advocate -----For the Plaintiff-Respondent-Petitioners. 
Shihab Uddin Ahmed, Advocate ----- For the Proforma-Defendant-Appellant-Opposite Parties.
parties:
Chowdhury Mia and others--------Plaintiff-Respondent-Petitioners
Vs.
Superintendent, Primary Teacher Institution and others-----Proforma-Defendant-Appellant-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J: These two rules, one under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure being Civil Revision No. 784 of 2007, another filed under Order XXXIX, Rule 2(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure being Civil Rule No. 364 (R) of 2007 (Violation) for violation of order of this Court arising out from the aforesaid Civil Revision No. 784 of 2008 are taken up together and this judgment would govern both these rules.

2. Petitioners as plaintiffs instituted the aforesaid Title Suit No. 137 of 1995 for permanent injunction. It is the case of plaintiffs that suit land originally belonged in 2 annas share to Hafiz Khatoon, wife of, Alimuddin, predecessor of plaintiffs. Fazil Mia is the son of Jorina Khatoon, sister of Hafiza Khatoon. Homestead of Fazil Mia was in south of Noakhali town. In 1919-20, Dhumchar was totally deluvated in the river. Hafiza Khatoon gifted 73 decimals of land to Fazil Mia in 1920 orally and delivered possession. Fazil Mia after constructing homestead, pond, latrine etc. possessing the same. Leter on, the land was reformed in situ. Defendant No. 3 through LA Case No. 2/1920-21, for constructing infrastructure of District Headquarters, Noakhali acquired the land, took possession of acquired land excepting the land of Fazil Mia as there was no registered deed of gift and there was homestead. Later on, Government did not evict the plaintiff from the suit land. Subsequently, Government decided not to transfer District Head quarters of Noakhali in the land acquired and land remain unused. Fazil Mia having no other land continued to stay on the gifted land from 1920 and excavated a pond at south west and another at north, constructed homestead on 8 decimals of land, to the south of the said pond is the road. With the earth of the said pond some other constructions were made by Fazil Mia. Fazil Mia along with family lived in the said homestead. Fazil Mia died, leaving 4 sons, plaintiff Nos. 1-4, 5-6 as daughters and 7 as wife. Later on, Pourashava holding was opened in the name of plaintiff Nos. 1-4 and 5-7. They regularly paid taxes and got receipts and also became voters and casted votes. Defendant No. I tried to construct boundary wall, whereupon plaintiffs filed application before the Government. District Kanango Investigated the matter and submitted report mentioning that there is homestead of plaintiffs but the matter was still under consideration before defendant No.3. Defendant No.3 by memo dated 15- 12-1993 directed defendant No. 1 to take step in the matter. On 28-4-1995 defendant No.1 came to the door of plaintiffs and tried to erect pucca wall, hence the suit.

3. The case make out by defendant No. 1 in its written statement is that the land was acquired in 1920 for defendant No. 2 for installing PTI. Public Works Department of Government constructed a building and the same was handed over to Primary Teacher Institution, PTI, on 28-1-1975 as per Government rules and regulation. In LA Case No. 2/1920-21 Government acquired 339 acres of land put since 1963 there having no development work, taking advantage of such situation, plaintiffs went into possession forcefully on the land of dag No. 108 which is totally illegal. Plaintiffs after getting forceful possession, digged ponds and filled some portion of the land of the aforesaid dag, constructed homestead. PTI went to evict the illegal occupant, tried but could not. Plaintiffs being illegal occupant, the suit should be dismissed with cost.

4. In the suit, plaintiff examined 4 witnesses and defendant examined 1 witness, beside plaintiff exhibited some documents.

5. Learned Judge of the trial court decreed the suit. Learned Judge of the appellate court dismissed the suit in allowing the appeal.

6. In decreeing the suit, learned Judge of the trial court found that, plaintiffs are in possession for more than 70 years. In dismissing the suit the learned Judge of the appellate court relied on the case of Belayet Hossain vs Nurul Alam, 42 DLR (AD) 20, where it is held that "A person in wrongful possession of property is not entitled to be protected against the lawful owner by an order of injunction and a trespasser is not entitled to perpetual injunction' against the owner of property," and, subsequently dismissed the suit.

7. Mr Abu Yahia Dulal, learned Advocate, appeared for the plaintiffs-petitioners, submits that, in a case of permanent injunction the court cannot decide title of the parties, possession is prime consideration that having not been denied by defendant as well as both the courts below having found possession of plaintiffs, the suit for permanent injunction ought to be decreed by the court of appeal below. Learned Advocate further submits that, plaintiffs cannot be said to be unauthorized occupant as Government after finding plaintiffs are in possession and constructed homestead, did not evict the plaintiffs in 1920, such possession of the plaintiffs being more than 70 years; they can maintain such possession till plaintiffs evicted by due process of law.

8. Learned Advocate in support of his submissions, relied on the case of Kaimuddin Shaikh alias Kaimu Shaikh vs Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Rajshahi, 3 BLC 410, the case of Jobayer Hossain vs Noor Hafez, 56 DLR (AD) 22, the case of Rafizuddin Ahmed vs Mongla Barman, 43 DLR (AD) 215, the case of Waziul Bashar (Md) vs Khaja Ahmed, 6 BLC 124, the case of Jabed Ali vs Abu Sheikh, being dead, his heirs Md Naimuddin, 1983 BLD (AD) 1=35 DLR (AD) 31, the case of Tajuddin vs Moktar Ahmed, 1991 BLD (AD) 144, the case of Farhaduzzaman vs Abdul Hasem Hawlader, 2 XP 81.

9. Mr Shihab Uddin Ahmed, learned Advocate, appearing for the defendant-appellant opposite parties, on the other hand, submits that, it is an admitted position that plaintiffs are in possession but their such possession being illegal, unauthorized cannot get any protection of law which having found by the court of appeal below committed no illegality in dismissing the suit while allowing the appeal.

10. Learned Advocate relied on the case of Administrative Officer, Housing Settlement, Chittagong vs Abdur Rashid Chowdhury, 63 DLR 479, the case of Abdul Kader Bhuiyan and 17 others vs Secretary, Ministry of Land, Government of the People s Republic of Bangladesh, 61 DLR (AD) 28, Rafizuddin Ahmed vs J. Mongla Barman, 43 DLR (AD) 215, the case of Dewan Shamsul Abedin, Mutwalli of Dewan Aftebur Reza Chowdhury Waqf Estate, of Village Tegharia, Police Station: Sunamgonj Sadar, District Sunamgonj, 13 MLR (AD) 163 = 13 DLR (AD) 118, the case. of Abdul Karim vs Bangladesh 51 DLR 447, the case of Belayet Hossain vs Nurul Alam Mir, 42 DLR (AD) 20, a case of granting of temporary injunction and also relied on section 16 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. We will refer the decisions after consideration of materials before us.

11. It is admitted position that plaintiffs are in possession from 1920 which is supported by the finding of the trial court but appellate court did not pass any reverse finding of the trial court on this score, but dismissed the suit holding that plaintiffs are in unauthorized possession. From written statement it appears defendant admitted possession of plaintiffs from 1962. In the written statement defendant stated that plaintiffs surreptitiously entered into possession taking advantage of the situation that no development work has been done in the acquired land and after acquiring the land in 1920, defendant goes as to show that plaintiffs are in possession to the very knowledge and notice of defendants. It is stated in written statement that that plaintiffs digged ponds, made homestead, filled earth and also dispossessed defendant PTI and make boundary wall. It is also the case of defendant that they tried to evict the plaintiffs but they did not proceed, further. The aforesaid facts i.e. digging of ponds, construction of homestead and filling of earth cannot be done in hiding and cannot be done hurriedly behind the back of defendant as all these work are time consuming. All these admitted facts established that plaintiffs, possession is hostile, notorious, actual, visible and exclusive.

12. Learned Judge of the appellate court took the view that unauthorized occupant cannot get any protection of law. Unauthorized occupant is a person who by force entered into possession and to maintain his possession, hasitly filed the suit for permanent injunction so that original owner may not evict him. In the case in hand the plaintiffs cannot be said to be unauthorized occupant or may not be said to be lawful occupant but they are in possession from 1920, this finding of trial court has not been reversed by the appellate court, by which the plaintiffs acquired at least possessory right which by lapse of time conferred them a kind of legality to maintain possession. In such admitted position, we are of the view that court of appeal below was not legal in not granting permanent injunction. Granting of injunction is a judicial process, by which one who has invaded or is threatening to invade the rights, legal or equitable, of another, is restrained from continuing or commencing such wrongful acts.

13. Decision cited by petitioners, particularly the cases of 56 DLR (AD) 22, 43 DLR (AD) 215, 1983 BLD (AD) 144, speaks that 'Even a trespasser's possession is good and valid against the entire world except the true owner and such possession is entitled to protection until he is evicted by due process of law.' We have also seen that long user of the suit land plaintiffs acquired a right of possession as such, he cannot to be thrown out of possession until and unless defendant could prove that they have better title over the land of plaintiffs by instituting properly constituted suit.

<u>14. Decision cited by the learned Advocate Mr Shihab Uddin Ahmed, accepting the case of Rafizuddin Ahmed vs Mongla Barman, 43 DLR (AD) 215, the case of Dewan Shamsul Abedin, Mutwalli of Dewan Aftebur Reza Chowdhury Waqf Estate, 13 MLR (AD) 163, the case of Belayet Hossain vs Nurul Alam Mir; 42 DLR (AD) 20, other decisions cited are not to be considered as in front of the Hon'ble Appellate Division's decision, the decisions of High Court Division should not be required to be looked into. The decisions as cited by the learned Advocate for the defendant if we consider in particular perspective then also these decisions support plaint case as in all these decisions it is held that for permanent injunction as regard dispute landed property the relief is available to a person who is in possession. The court may inquire incidentally into the respective claims of the parties to the suit for determining whether the plaintiff is in possession of the disputed property and are entitled to the specific relief of permanent injunction. 42 DLR (AD) case is a case on granting temporary injunction. Article 144 of Limitation Act provides 60 years possession to give title, over the land of Government. We have seen that Appellate Court did not disturb the finding of trial court's finding of plaintiffs' possession for 70 years. We find merit in the rule.</u>

15. In the result, the rule is made absolute without any order as to cost.

16. The judgment and decree dated 20-2-2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 200 Court, Noakhali in Title Appeal No. 212 of 2000 is set-aside and those of the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Noakhali in Title Suit No. 137 of 1995 is restored.

<u>17. Now to the second one. It is the case of plaintiffs petitioners that, while Rule was issued and injunction was granted, the violator, Superintendent of Primary Training Institute on taking advantage of the decision of the Appellate Court, dispossessed plaintiff on 14-5-2007. We find that violator Superintendent without any order from any court dismantled the property of plaintiffs. It is a heinous offence and should not go without any punishment but Mr Shihab Uddin Ahmed, learned Advocate, submits that, this woman, did it on the instruction of her superior authority against whom no Rule was issued. We do no understand how a superior authority could act in such a manner taking law in his own hand. The suit is filed by plaintiffs not by the defendants. The suit may be dismissed or may be decreed which cannot in any way prompt the defendant to evict the plaintiffs or dismantle the property taking recourse to force. When law is there, until and unless the law is invoked no one can evict from the suit property by administrative order, but since it is submitted on reference to the records that when dismantle was done violator was not in knowledge about pendency of the proceeding before the High Court Division. We exonerate her from charge but we are directing defendant to restore possession of the plaintiffs within 30 days from today. It has been submitted that the violator has already retired. In that case we direct the present Superintendent of PTI that he shall restore possession of the plaintiffs within 30 days from today, not from the date of receipt of this order. We further direct the Superintendent of PTI that if possession be not restored to the plaintiffs within 30 days then he shall pay as compensation, Taka 50,000 to the plaintiffs per day till Superintendent restore possession of the plaintiffs.</u>

18. With these observations the Rule being Civil Rule No. 364(R) of 2007 (Violation) is disposed of.

Send down the lower court records. Communicate this order at once.

End.
